description: A glitch processor: a sample-rate reducer, a low-pass filter, then a Schroeder reverb whose delay lines can be read at any speed, backwards included

params.text: Sets the feedback of the reverb's comb and allpass sections, over 0.1 to 0.99; the maker's tooltip prints this figure in seconds, which it is not
Sets the balance between the filtered signal and the reverb, over dry to fully wet; it comes up fully wet
Sets how many samples are held between each new sample taken, over 0 to 100; at 0 nothing is held and the signal passes straight through
Scales the redux CV before it is added, over -1 to 1, at which a full 5V moves the hold length by 50 samples
A latch that throws away the fractional part of the redux CV, so the hold length moves in steps of ten samples
Sets the corner of the low-pass filter the signal meets before the reverb, over 20Hz to 10kHz; it comes up at 10kHz
Sets the rate at which the reverb's delay lines are read, over -2 to 2, where 1 is the writing rate, 0 holds them and negative values read backwards

inputs.text: The signal fed into the sample-rate reducer, and from there into the filter and the reverb
Adds to the hold length through its attenuverter; the total is clamped to 0 and 100 samples

outputs.text: The reverb output, with no clamp applied to it

notes: The module declares a Speed CV input and an attenuverter for it, and draws neither on the panel, so the read speed can be set only by its knob.
The redux control comes up at 0, which holds nothing, so the sample-rate reduction does nothing until it is turned up.

inputs.0:
bipolar · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
inputs.1:
continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
